items.title: Scientex to acquire 70pct interest in China's Mintpack for RM102mil
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Scientex Bhd, through its wholly-owned subsidiary Scientex Packaging (Ayer Keroh) Bhd (SPAK), has entered into a sale and purchase agreement to acquire a 70 per cent stake in China-based Hunan Changcheng Mint New Material Technology Co., Ltd. ("Mintpack"). The proposed acquisition involves a purchase consideration of RMB167.3 million, approximately RM101.5 million, said Scientex in a filing with Bursa Malaysia on Tuesday. Scientex views the acquisition as a strategic avenue to expand the group's consumer packaging footprint into China.

items.title: Why do so many Malaysians ride motorcycles?
items.summary: FOR many riders, the motorcycle is solving a practical problem. In 2024, 78.1 per cent of Malaysian households owned a motorcycle. For that rider, the motorcycle is not simply transport.

items.title: Missing Orang Asli woman found dead in Rompin swamp
items.summary: ROMPIN: The search for a missing 73-year-old Orang Asli woman ended today when her body was found in a swampy area in Kampung Lesung, Kedaik, police said. The remains of Kuang Poh, who was last seen leaving her home for a fishing trip on Sept 22, were found at 11.50am. Rompin district police chief Superintendent Sharif Shai Sharif Mondoi said search and rescue (SAR) team members found Kuang's decomposed remains about 500 metres from where she was last seen.

items.title: PN seeks RoS clarification on use of coalition logo in Melaka election
items.summary: KOTA BHARU: Perikatan Nasional (PN) has written to the Registrar of Societies (RoS) seeking clarification on whether it can use the coalition's logo in the Melaka election. "We have written to RoS to seek clarification on whether the Perikatan Nasional logo can be used in the Melaka election. In an election, any party can use another party's logo.

items.title: Vantris recorded RM75mil fourth-consecutive quarterly net profits in Q2
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Vantris Energy Bhd reported net profit of RM75.3 million in the second quarter ended July 31, 2026 (Q2 FY27) – its fourth consecutive quarter in the black – despite registering lower revenue. The turnaround from the corresponding quarter last year was driven by lower foreign exchange losses, the absence of a favourable insurance claim recorded in the previous corresponding quarter and lower finance costs following the completion of the company's restructuring exercise. Revenue for the quarter fell 22.8 per cent to RM818 million from RM1.06 billion, mainly due to lower contributions from the engineering and construction (E&C) segment.

items.title: KLIA workers, community to get priority access during Sepang F1
items.summary: Selangor police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said access would be maintained via Lebuh Madani, Charterfield Roundabout and Jalan CTA 2 during the championship at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) from Oct 2 to 4. Shazeli said SIC would have parking capacity for 9,000 cars across 17 parking lots, with spaces allocated at any one time according to designated categories. To facilitate visitor movement, free shuttle bus and e-hailing services would also be provided from various locations to SIC.

items.title: French teens clash with police as school blockades intensify
items.summary: PARIS: French teenagers on Tuesday set fire to rubbish bins and hurled projectiles in clashes with police, as they kept up a blockade of some high schools demanding better conditions at their establishments but which has angered the government. High school students have since last week staged protests outside their schools over grievances including timetables, class sizes and a shortage of teachers as well as overheated classrooms in the wake of the recent heatwaves. Masked students gathered outside the Lycee Cesar Baggio in Lille, in northern France, setting bins on fire, an AFP photographer reported.

items.title: UN concerned by Malaysia returns of Myanmar migrants
items.summary: GENEVA, Sept 29 — The UN voiced worry today over Malaysia’s decision to send 1,500 Myanmar nationals back to the war-torn country, stressing that conditions there “do not permit safe, dignified and sustainable returns”. “We are concerned by the reported imminent return of some 1,500 individuals from Myanmar to that country,” United Nations refugee agency spokesman Matthew Saltmarsh told reporters in Geneva, insisting that “under international law, no one should be sent to a country where they may face persecution, torture, serious harm, or other threats to life, liberty, and security”. — AFP

items.title: Undocumented Bajau Laut youths face exploitation in Sabah
items.summary: SEMPORNA: Undocumented Bajau Laut youths in Sabah face exploitation and limited employment opportunities as changes to their traditional sea-based livelihoods add to their challenges. The Bajau Laut are a traditionally sea-based community in Sabah, with some members among the state's undocumented population, lacking official documents. I didn't want the problem to get worse," said Bob, a pseudonym used to protect his identity.

items.title: [UPDATED] 'Where do we put them?': Anwar defends Myanmar talks, demands safety guarantees for refugees
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has defended Malaysia's engagement with Myanmar, saying calls to simply "not send them back" offer no solution for the hundreds of thousands of Myanmar refugees in the country. He said Malaysia was seeking security guarantees for any returns, which was why Myanmar President Min Aung Hlaing had been invited for talks. That is why we invited him (Min Aung Hlaing) to negotiate," he said.

items.title: Cocaine evidence missing from Fiji court was swapped out for flour, media say
items.summary: SYDNEY: Several kilogrammes of cocaine held as evidence in a major Fiji drug case have gone missing from a court, police said on Tuesday, with media saying the drug, valued at about US$31 million, was swapped out for flour. The drug exhibits stolen from the High Court in Suva, the capital of the Pacific island nation, amounted to nearly 40 kg, media said. The Fiji Village news outlet said the remaining 32 bars had been filled with flour.

items.title: German security agencies face dilemma after victories for far right and far left
items.summary: THIS month's victories for far-right and far-left parties in German state elections have intensified official debate over whether security authorities can restrict secret information that might be passed on to Russia or criminal groups. The far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) party, which came close to winning an absolute majority in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt on Sept 6, and the far-left Left Party, which came first in the capital Berlin on Sept 20, could both pose risks, senior figures in the ruling coalition say. "This concerns information relating to organised crime – that would be an issue in Berlin," said Alexander Hoffmann, head of the parliamentary group of the Christian Social Union (CSU), the Bavarian sister party of Chancellor Friedrich Merz's Christian Democrats (CDU).

items.title: Heavy vehicles to be diverted around Sepang during F1 Bahrain GP weekend
items.summary: Selangor police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said the diversion would be carried out by the Selangor police contingent's Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department (TEID), together with the Road Transport Department (RTD). "Among the checkpoints are Masjid Roundabout, Jalan KLIA S8, Jalan B48, Persiaran Teknologi 1 and 2, and Jalan Besar Salak," he said in a statement. Shazeli said TEID would also operate five main screening locations for ticket and vehicle-pass checks.

items.title: [UPDATED] Why single out Loke when corruption is real problem, asks Anwar
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has questioned why Anthony Loke was being singled out over his offer to resign as transport minister. Anwar said corruption and plunder were the nation's real issues, rather than Loke's resignation. "This issue of Anthony Loke... what is the problem?

items.title: 822 police, RTD personnel deployed for F1 Bahrain GP
items.summary: Selangor police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said the deployment comprised 756 policemen including 391 general-duty personnel and 365 traffic personnel, supported by 66 RTD officers. The inner zone, covering areas within two kilometres, includes Jalan Pekeliling, Jalan Kuarters, Jalan Besar Salak and Jalan B48 Kampung Chincang. "The middle zone, covering three to five kilometres, includes the KLIA Expressway, Jalan Labohan Dagang, Jalan Pekeliling and Jalan KLIA 1.

items.title: S&P reaffirms Malaysia's A- rating, stable outlook
items.summary: The Finance Ministry said S&P also pointed to Malaysia's gradual fiscal consolidation, strong monetary policy flexibility and historically supportive external position. The "Stable" outlook reflects S&P's expectation that Malaysia's growth momentum and current policy environment will support steady fiscal performance over the next two to three years, the ministry said in a statement today. S&P expects Malaysia's economy to expand 5.5 per cent in 2026, following 5.2 per cent growth in 2025 and 5.7 per cent year-on-year expansion in the first half of this year.

items.title: Myanmar airstrike toll hits 50 as families gather dead
items.summary: KYAUKTAW: Families searched for bodies on Tuesday around a charred market in western Myanmar after a military airstrike killed 50 people, one of the deadliest recent bombardments in the civil war. Witnesses say the military's air force raided the riverside commercial hub in Kyauktaw town in western Rakhine state around midday (0530 GMT) on Monday. "It breaks my heart to see our people dying," said Aung Chay, still hunting for the remains of his brother-in-law he believes was killed in the attack.

items.title: Khalid: PH-BN cooperation was never based on shared political goals
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Pakatan Harapan and Barisan Nasional have distinct political cultures and directions, with their cooperation in the unity government aimed solely at maintaining stability. Amanah communications director Khalid Abdul Samad said BN's statement that its cooperation with the unity government will end once Parliament is dissolved comes as no surprise. "To achieve stability following the 15th General Election (GE15), the unity government was formed despite involving two very different political entities.

items.title: Rapid Bus tests 5 electric buses on Sunway BRT ahead of 250-bus rollout
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Rapid Bus Sdn Bhd, a subsidiary of Prasarana Malaysia Bhd, is testing five electric buses on the Sunway Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) line ahead of the rollout of 250 new electric buses. In a statement today, Rapid Bus said the phased procurement of the new electric buses was part of its efforts to enhance public transport services through modern, energy-efficient and sustainable technology. Rapid Bus chief executive officer Syahrul Azmir Ahmad Zaki said the trials were a crucial step towards ensuring smooth electric bus operations before the fleet was deployed on other routes.

items.title: Two men jailed 30 years for trafficking 139kg cannabis in Bangsar
items.summary: Judge Datuk Mohd Arief Emran Arifin sentenced S. Mohan, 38, and Ahmad Shamil Abdul Rashid, 28, after ruling that the prosecution had proven its case beyond a reasonable doubt. Mohan and Ahmad Shamil were charged with jointly trafficking 139,019.3 grammes of cannabis a shopping complex car park in Bangsar about 2pm on May 31, 2022. Lawyer Muhammad Faiz Fadzil, representing Ahmad Shamil, said his client had also been in custody since his arrest.

items.title: Johor RTD investigates foreigners renting cars to operate 'kereta sapu' services
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: The Johor Road Transport Department (RTD) is investigating allegations that foreigners were renting cars from Malaysians and using them to operate illegal e-hailing and "kereta sapu" services in several districts in the state. The clip also showed a Malaysian confronting the foreign driver, who was allegedly driving a vehicle without a valid driving licence, e-hailing permit and road tax. He said RTD had issued a notice under Section 114 of the Road Transport Act 1987 to the registered owner of the vehicle, requiring the person to appear at the department to facilitate investigations.

items.title: Iran's Revolutionary Guards call Trump a 'big liar'
items.summary: Meanwhile, Iran's parliamentary speaker said that no country in the region would be able to export oil if the Islamic Republic was prevented from selling its own oil, state media reported.' No regional infrastructure would be safe if Iran had no security, Mohammad Baqer Ghalibaf added, according to the reports. Ghalibaf also said that if his country's security was not guaranteed, no infrastructure in the region would be safe from attack, state media reported.

items.title: PH rules out cooperation with BN for Melaka polls
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Pakatan Harapan will not partner with Barisan Nasional for the upcoming 16th Melaka election. Amanah communications director Khalid Abdul Samad said PH has decided on the matter and remains open to collaborating with any other party except BN and Perikatan Nasional (PN). Commenting on potential cooperation between PH and Bersatu, Khalid, who is also a former Federal Territories minister, said Bersatu must understand PH's principles, which emphasise performance, integrity, and values.

items.title: Smart lights to respond to Kulai traffic in real time
items.summary: KULAI: Motorists in Indahpura could soon spend less time waiting at traffic lights as Kulai Municipal Council trials a smart traffic system designed to adjust signal timings according to real-time traffic conditions. Johor Housing and Local Government Committee chairman Datuk Mohd Jafni Md Shukor said the system was being trialled at the Bandar Putra-Indahpura interchange, with its effectiveness to be measured by how much it could reduce journey times and vehicle queues. Jafni said the system could also coordinate signals between junctions to improve traffic flow across multiple intersections, while its operation could be monitored in real time through the Kulai Integrated Command, Control and Communication Centre.

items.title: Women’s ministry: Victims of sexual harassment need to speak up, no shame in it
items.summary: BUTTERWORTH, Sept 29 —The Ministry of Women, Family and Community Development (KPWKM) is calling on students to know their boundaries, dare to say no, and seek help if they face sexual harassment or violence. We also want to teach them how to seek help when someone faces sexual harassment or violence. Lim said bullying, sexual harassment and violence require a cross-ministry approach, covering advocacy, prevention, awareness and counselling.

items.title: Heavy rain, gusty winds expected across peninsula and Sarawak until 7pm, warns MetMalaysia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 29 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a thunderstorm warning for several states in Peninsular Malaysia and Sarawak, with thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds expected until 7pm today. In Peninsular Malaysia, the warning covers Penang, Perak and Melaka, as well as parts of five other states. In Sarawak, the warning covers Sri Aman, Betong, Sarikei (Sarikei and Maradong), Sibu (Sibu), Samarahan (Sebuyau) and Kapit (Song).

items.title: Retired soldier fined RM4,000 for false birth registration
items.summary: KUANTAN: A retired soldier was fined RM4,000 by the magistrate's court after pleading guilty to providing false information when registering his child's birth 19 years ago. He was charged with providing false information when filling out a birth registration form, resulting in the issuance of a birth certificate for the child. Fauzi submitted the birth registration form for his child, along with the maternal health record book, at the registaration department's counter on Dec 4, 2007.

items.title: Woman found unconscious behind a building in Sabah dies
items.summary: PENAMPANG, Sept 29 — A 38-year-old local woman died after she was found unconscious on the ground behind a building in Donggongon here yesterday. Penampang police chief Supt Sammy Newton said police received a report on the incident at about 12.36pm. Those with information are urged to contact the investigating officer, Penampang police station chief Insp Ahmad Amir Fitri Ab Rahman at 016-449 2215.

items.title: CAAM: Don't be alarmed by low-flying aircraft over Sepang
items.summary: The Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) said the operations would take place between 2pm and 3pm on the scheduled dates, with aircraft expected to fly at lower altitudes than usual. Earlier, CAAM deputy chief executive officer Zainul Abidin Maslan said a low-level flypast by a Gulf Air Boeing 787 Dreamliner was expected to wow crowds at the race. Zainul said the flypast had been coordinated between CAAM's air traffic control centre and the Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) control tower.

items.title: Over 100 settlers attack West Bank village, injuring Israeli forces
items.summary: RAMALLAH: More than 100 Israeli settlers attacked a village in the north of the occupied West Bank early Tuesday, wounding three members of Israel's security forces and burning two Palestinian homes, authorities and residents said. Tuesday's assault received rare strong criticism from Israeli officials, while police said they had arrested one individual and taken two minors in for questioning. The Israeli military said "more than 100 Israeli rioters" were in the area of Jalud overnight as security forces attempted to return the family to their home, adding that soldiers and border police forces had operated to disperse the settlers.

items.title: Gulf Air Dreamliner flypast to wow F1 crowds at Sepang
items.summary: SEPANG: A low-level flypast by a Gulf Air Boeing 787 Dreamliner is expected to wow crowds at the Sepang International Circuit as the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix Malaysia 2026 gets underway on Sunday. Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) deputy chief executive officer Zainul Abidin Maslan said the flypast had been coordinated between CAAM's Air Traffic Control Centre and the Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) control tower. That has been coordinated by both the Kuala Lumpur Air Traffic Control Centre and the KLIA control tower.

items.title: Ismail Lasim leaves palace after three-hour audience with Tuanku Muhriz
items.summary: SEREMBAN: Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim concluded a nearly three-hour audience with Yang di-Pertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir at Istana Hinggap here today. Ismail, who arrived at 10.50am for the 11am audience, left the palace grounds via the back gate, avoiding media members gathered outside. Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi had previously directed Ismail to seek an audience with Tuanku Muhriz to address the ongoing custom crisis.

items.title: Serian tops API readings as 33 areas record unhealthy levels
items.summary: In Sarawak, Samarahan and Kuching recorded 159 each, followed by Sri Aman at 133. Cheras and Batu Muda recorded 169 and 155 respectively, while Putrajaya recorded 164. In Terengganu, Kuala Terengganu recorded 127, followed by Kemaman at 104.

items.title: Tokyo suffers longest streak of rainy days on record
items.summary: TOKYO: Tokyo has logged 34 straight days of rain, marking the longest streak on record, Japan's weather agency said on Tuesday. Climate change fuelled by fossil fuel emissions increases moisture in the atmosphere, making heavy rain more likely. "Autumn rain fronts are staying longer than usual," Kyoda said, referring to Tokyo's rainy season, because a high pressure system in the Pacific is also remaining longer than normal.

items.title: DVS tests 18 dogs following rabies scare in Kedah’s Changlun
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 29 — The Kedah Department of Veterinary Services (DVS) has collected samples from 18 dogs in Changlun, Kedah, and surrounding areas for rabies confirmatory testing as of yesterday, following an incident where a man was bitten by a stray dog in the area. Subsequently, Kedah DVS conducted an on-site investigation and carried out operations to capture stray dogs in collaboration with the Kubang Pasu Municipal Council to locate the suspected animal and assess the potential presence of the rabies virus. Kedah DVS is continuing its investigation and awaiting laboratory results to confirm the presence of rabies among dogs in Kedah,” the statement read.

items.title: Home Ministry: 1,476 Myanmar nationals leave Malaysia in first ‘voluntary’ repatriation phase
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 29 — A total of 1,476 Myanmar nationals departed Malaysia today under the first phase of a “voluntary” repatriation programme aimed at resolving a protracted, decades-long refugee and undocumented migrant challenge, the Home Ministry (KDN) announced. The operation is being conducted by sea via two naval vessels and a hospital ship deployed by the Myanmar government, coordinated jointly by KDN, the Immigration Department of Malaysia (JIM), and relevant security agencies. KDN stated that as of Aug 15, a total of 10,388 Myanmar nationals held across Immigration detention depots nationwide have been undergoing biometric identification, immigration status assessments, and security screenings.

items.title: MACC: Ex-senior exec to be charged over RM42m UiTM Holdings loss
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 29 — A former senior executive of a corporation will be charged in court this Thursday in connection with the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) investigation into losses incurred by UiTM Holdings Sdn Bhd, including allegations of abuse of power regarding operational expense payments to several companies totalling about RM42 million. “The arrest follows an investigation conducted by MACC regarding issues concerning losses suffered by UiTM Holdings Sdn Bhd (UiTM Holdings) in 2023,” the statement read. Meanwhile, MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman confirmed the arrest when contacted and stated that the case is being investigated under Section 23 of the MACC Act 2009.

items.title: Guan Eng says foreign workers should be excluded from minimum wage hike, calls for EPF levy repeal
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 29 — DAP chairman Lim Guan Eng today called on the government to exclude foreign workers from any increase in Malaysia’s minimum wage, arguing that the move would help protect local businesses, particularly micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), from rising operating costs. While acknowledging the rationale for higher wages, Lim said the prospect of a minimum wage increase has sparked concern among local businesses already grappling with intense competition, higher compliance costs and taxes, as well as price pressures from overseas producers. According to Lim, exempting foreign workers from minimum wage increases and scrapping the EPF contribution requirement would help ease cost pressures on local businesses and safeguard the viability of approximately 1.2 million MSMEs nationwide.

items.title: Public to get live access to Sabah 40pc revenue appeal at Kota Kinabalu court
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 29 — Up to 250 members of the public will be able to follow the Court of Appeal hearing on Sabah’s constitutional 40 per cent revenue entitlement next month through a live audiovisual transmission at the Kota Kinabalu Court Complex. The arrangement will allow members of the public to watch the proceedings from the court’s conference hall while the appeal is heard inside the courtroom on Oct 29. The Court of Appeal is scheduled to hear the federal government’s appeal against the High Court’s October 17, 2025 decision in the judicial review brought by the Sabah Law Society (SLS).

items.title: Marina Mahathir: My father healthy but lonely after loss of beloved wife
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 29 — Former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad is coping with a deep sense of loneliness following the death of his wife, Tun Dr Hasmah Mohd Ali, whom he shared more than seven decades of marriage with, according to their daughter, Datuk Marina Mahathir. Berita Harian reported that Marina said her 101-year-old father remains in good health but is grieving the loss of his lifelong companion, who died yesterday at the age of 100. He feels lonely,” Marina told reporters after visiting Dr Hasmah’s grave at Pusara Negara in Presint 20 today.

items.title: Dr M recalls shock at wife Dr Hasmah’s sudden passing despite signs of good health
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Sept 29 — Former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad has said he did not expect his wife, Tun Dr Hasmah Ali, to pass away yesterday, recalling that she had appeared to be in good health the night before. Dr Mahathir also thanked the royal family for making the journey from Pahang to offer their condolences. Dr Hasmah died at about 9.25am yesterday at the National Heart Institute.

items.title: Nanta: New Johor Bahru court complex among 11 judicial projects worth RM736m nationwide
items.summary: ISKANDAR PUTERI, Sept 29 — The new Johor Bahru court complex in Kota Iskandar is among 11 judicial infrastructure projects being developed nationwide with a cumulative value of RM736 million, Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi said today. “The Johor Bahru court complex project was approved by the Economic Planning Unit (EPU) of the Prime Minister's Department back in 2018 under the 11th Malaysia Plan. Also present at the event was Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said.

items.title: Fahmi: Only register for medicine delivery service through MoH to avoid scams on Facebook, TikTok
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 29 — Applications for the government's medicine delivery service (UMP) should be done only through the Ministry of Health, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said today as he cautioned against possible scam attempts. "I remind everyone there is no registration process other than at health clinics or Ministry of Health facilities only." Patients in Malaysia will soon be able to receive their follow-up medication delivered directly to their doorstep free of charge, following a joint funding initiative announced today by the Communications Ministry and the Health Ministry.

items.title: PM Anwar congratulates Kelantan Sultan on 57th birthday
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 29 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim extended his heartfelt congratulations to the Sultan of Kelantan, Sultan Muhammad V, on the occasion of the ruler’s 57th birthday. In a Facebook post today, Anwar prayed that Sultan Muhammad V and the entire royal family will always be blessed with His grace and guidance. Daulat Tuanku,” he said.

items.title: Health minister: Mission is to transform healthcare within 15th Parliament timeframe
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 29 — Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad wants the national healthcare transformation agenda, including modernising the system and improving patient service delivery, to be completed within the 15th parliamentary term. He said the Ministry of Health (MOH) faces a major challenge of not only keeping facilities ready but also ensuring healthcare delivery consistently meets the people’s needs. Dzulkefly said MOH faces increasingly complex challenges, including food safety and quality, mental health and planetary health.

items.title: Lawmakers welcome national suicide registry, urge strict service standards for crisis helplines
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 29 — Three DAP lawmakers have welcomed the launch of the National Suicide and Fatal Injury Registry Malaysia (NSFIRM) and the Ministry of Health’s Postvention Services Guidelines, while calling for stronger crisis helpline standards. In a joint statement, Bandar Kuching MP Dr Kelvin Yii Lee Wuen and state assemblymen Lim Yi Wei (Kampung Tunku) and Michelle Ng Mei Sze (Subang Jaya) said the launch, three years after attempted suicide was decriminalised, reaffirms the government’s commitment to mental health. They said that Malaysia previously lacked a systematic registry of suicide deaths and attempts.

items.title: Perak PKR chairman Mohamad Hairul Amir sworn in as senator
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 29 — Perak PKR chairman Mohamad Hairul Amir Sabri today took his oath of office as a Senator representing the state for a three-year term from Sept 10, 2026 to Sept 9, 2029. Mohamad Hairul Amir, 38, was sworn in before Dewan Negara President Datuk Awang Bemee Awang Ali Basah at a ceremony held at the Senate here. Meanwhile, Awang Bemee, in his speech, said Mohamad Hairul Amir’s broad experience spanning political leadership, public administration, government relations, community development and corporate governance would bring valuable insights to Senate debates and proceedings.

items.title: Loke: Transport Ministry to centralise bunkering licences from February 2027
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 29 — The Transport Ministry will assume sole authority for approving bunkering licences and related permits starting February 1, 2027. Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook said that centralising these approvals will provide operators with a single point of accountability and ensure more consistent decisions regarding safety, fuel quality, and environmental protection. This will help to boost our bunkering sector, hopefully,” Loke said while officiating Malaysia Maritime Week 2026 at the Kuala Lumpur Convention Centre.

items.title: PM: Malaysians should have the choice to work past 60, ageing population needs options
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 29 — With Malaysia expected to be an aged nation by 2048, the focus should not only be on ensuring sufficient retirement savings but also ensuring people have the choice to work past age 60, the prime minister said today. In Malaysia, the minimum retirement age for the private sector and the mandatory retirement age for civil servants are both currently at age 60. In his speech, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said those who want to work after age 60 should be given the choice, but did not say whether there are plans to raise the minimum or mandatory retirement age.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan MB meets Tuanku Muhriz amid royal dispute
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Sept 29 — Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim was reportedly granted an audience with Yang di-Pertuan Besar Negeri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir at Istana Hinggap here today amid the state’s ongoing constitutional and customary dispute. The meeting was also understood to have been attended by Undang Luak Sungei Ujong Datuk Klana Petra Muhammad Faris Johari, Undang Luak Rembau Datuk Sedia Raja Hassan Ab Hamid and Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad. Barisan Nasional chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi had recently urged Ismail to meet Tuanku Muhriz and the Undang Yang Empat to seek a resolution to the dispute.

items.title: Loke says will stay as transport minister until Najib house arrest begins
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 29 — Anthony Loke Siew Fook today said that he will stay on as transport minister until former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak begins his house arrest. He said that he had submitted his resignation letter to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim yesterday, when they had discussed the matter further. So, the timeframe is that when Najib returns home, my resignation will take effect,” Loke told reporters after officiating Malaysia Maritime Week 2026 at the Kuala Lumpur Convention Centre.

items.title: High Court finds Putrajaya, Selangor authorities liable for Taman Sri Muda flood devastation
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Sept 29 — The High Court has found the Malaysian government liable for damages caused by the catastrophic 2021 floods that devastated Taman Sri Muda in Shah Alam, citing a failure to promptly escalate disaster response and maintain effective mitigation systems. The court also found the director-general of the Selangor Department of Irrigation and Drainage (DID) and the Shah Alam City Council (MBSA) jointly liable with the federal government. The court rejected the defendants’ attempt to use an “act of God” defence, ruling it inapplicable when reasonable human intervention could have mitigated the disaster.

items.title: Avoid the F1 rush: AirAsia advises extra KLIA travel time Oct 2-4
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 29 — AirAsia advises all guests travelling through the Kuala Lumpur International Airport Terminal 2 to plan their journey, as higher passenger volumes and heavier traffic are expected in conjunction with the Formula 1 race weekend at Sepang International Circuit from Oct 2 to 4. The airlines said guests are advised to arrive at the airport at least three hours before the scheduled departure time for international flights and two hours before the scheduled departure time for domestic flights. “All guests, including those travelling under group bookings, are strongly encouraged to complete self check-in via the AirAsia MOVE app or our website.

items.title: Malaysia targets 60pc of EPF members reaching RM390,000 savings by 2030
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 29 — Malaysia aims to increase the Retirement Income Adequacy framework to six in 10 Employees Provident Fund (EPF) members to reach the ‘Basic Savings’ benchmark of RM390,000 by age 60 by 2030. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said currently, close to four in 10 members are now on track to reach the benchmark under the EPF’s Retirement Income Adequacy framework. Anwar’s speech was read by Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan.

items.title: Fahmi Fadzil plays down Pakatan-Bersatu Melaka dinner
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 29 — Communication Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said today he has little information about a supposed closed-door dinner attended by Pakatan Harapan and Bersatu leaders in Melaka last night. Among Bersatu leaders sighted at the dinner were information chief Datuk Tun Faisal Ismail Aziz, the party's state election director Datuk Seri Mohamad Ali Mohamad, associate wing vice-chief and supreme council member Datuk Seri R. Sanjeevan and Melaka Bersatu information chief Datuk Hishamuddin Abdul Karim. On PH side were Melaka Amanah chairman Datuk Ashraf Mukhlis Minghat and acting state PKR chairman Adam Adli Abdul Halim.

items.title: Hazy conditions descend on Malaysia again as 31 areas hit ‘Unhealthy’ API
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 29 — A total of 31 areas nationwide recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as at 9 am today. According to the Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, the areas included the Serian Police headquarters in Sarawak with the air pollutant index at 175; Pasir Gudang (170) and Larkin (169) in Johor; Bandaraya Melaka (166); Nilai, Negeri Sembilan (165); Johan Setia, Selangor (163); and Batu Muda in the capital (114). Thirty areas had a moderate API reading while seven areas had a good API reading.

items.title: Former Felda Investment CEO charged with cheating board over RM500m Jalan Semarak land deal
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 29 — A former chief executive officer of Felda Investment Corporation Sdn Bhd (FIC) was charged in the Sessions Court here today with two counts of deceiving the company’s board of directors over the commercial development of Felda land along Jalan Semarak in 2014. On the first count, Zaid is accused of deceiving the FIC board into believing that Synergy Promenade Sdn Bhd was qualified for appointment as the project’s master developer, despite knowing the company was only eligible to serve as its master planner. On the second count, Zaid is accused of deceiving the FIC board regarding the commercial valuation of 24 lots of Felda land by misrepresenting that a market assessment by Firdaus & Associates Property Professionals Sdn Bhd valued the development at RM330.96 million, when the valuer's actual reported assessment was RM691.7 million.

items.title: Marine police, Perhilitan seize RM700,000 worth of protected birds in Terengganu
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU, Sept 29 — The Kuala Terengganu Region Three Marine Police Force (PPM) and Terengganu Wildlife and National Parks Department (Perhilitan) seized more than 50 protected birds and 60 cages worth RM709,950 in an integrated operation near Kampung Binjai Manis, Manir, here Sunday. PPM Region Three commander ACP Mohd Khairuddin Jamal said all the birds found during the operation yesterday afternoon were protected species under the Wildlife Conservation Act 2010 (Act 716). Khairuddin said the operation involved personnel from the Kuala Terengganu and Tasik Kenyir sectors of the Region Three Marine Police Force, as well as 14 Terengganu Perhilitan officers.

items.title: Police nab two men ‘chauffeuring’ 690kg of ketum in Toyota Alphard on NSE
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 29 — Two local men were arrested after allegedly possessing 690 kilogrammes of ketum leaves in a car at KM371 of the North-South Expressway (PLUS) southbound early yesterday. He said the two suspects were believed to be runners supplying ketum leaves for the local market. Khalid said preliminary checks found that the first suspect had one drug-related record and five criminal records, while the second had two drug-related records and one criminal record.

items.title: PM lauds Malaysian contingent on best WorldSkills showing since 1995
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 29 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim congratulated the Malaysian contingent for winning one bronze medal and 13 Medallions for Excellence at the WorldSkills Competition (WSC) Shanghai 2026. Anwar said the achievement was the national contingent’s best performance in the competition since 1995. “Continue to hone your skills and pursue excellence.
